hints.title: Adjacency Graph Degrees
hints.text: Build an undirected adjacency list where every internal number has degree 2 and the two endpoints have degree 1.

hints.title: Identify Starting Endpoint
hints.text: Find a vertex with degree 1 to serve as the start of the reconstructed sequence.

hints.title: Follow Path Linearly
hints.text: Traverse the list from the start node, moving to each unvisited neighbor until all n numbers are reconstructed.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def restoreArray(self, adjacentPairs: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        for u, v in adjacentPairs:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)

        start = None
        for node, neighbors in adj.items():
            if len(neighbors) == 1:
                start = node
                break

        n = len(adjacentPairs) + 1
        res = [start]
        prev = None
        curr = start
        for _ in range(n - 1):
            nxt = adj[curr][0] if adj[curr][0] != prev else adj[curr][1]
            res.append(nxt)
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        return res
```

variables: n is length of restored array
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Permuting or searching pairs naively takes quadratic or exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency list traversal reconstructs the path in linear O(n) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate identifies endpoint condition (degree 1) and walks the path avoiding backwards steps.
